headline: Jushi agrees $6.5M Illinois grow deal to go vertical in a sixth state
dek: Jushi Holdings said on 24 November it will buy an Illinois cultivation and processing site for $6.5 million and seek up to $20 million for Virginia growth.
key_points: A Jushi subsidiary agreed to buy an Illinois cultivation and processing facility, with licences and assets, for $6.5 million in cash, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027.
Its lender consented to the deal and may provide up to $4.25 million in extra term loans, which Jushi expects to be funded on or about 4 December 2026.
Jushi is negotiating to expand its Manassas, Virginia mortgage by up to $15–20 million toward a roughly $40 million build-out ahead of Virginia's 1 July 2027 adult-use start.
Preliminary October net revenue rose 4.6% to about $23.4 million, while gross margin widened to 48.6% from 41.9%.
body: Jushi Holdings plans to become a vertically integrated operator in Illinois. In a business update released on 24 November, the Boca Raton-based multistate operator said one of its subsidiaries has agreed to buy a cultivation and processing facility in the state, together with its licences and related assets, for $6.5 million in cash. The deal still needs regulatory approval and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

The same release set out a financing plan built around Virginia, where Jushi is expanding its Manassas grow ahead of adult-use sales, and a preliminary look at October trading that showed modest sales growth and a sharp improvement in gross margin. Jushi trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange and the OTCQX under the symbol JUSH.
## What Jushi is buying in Illinois

Jushi already runs four Beyond Hello dispensaries in Illinois. Adding its own cultivation and processing would make Illinois the company's sixth vertically integrated state, according to the release. Jushi also said the acquired facility would have capacity to supply up to six more dispensaries, which points to room for retail growth in the state rather than only a cost play on wholesale purchases.

The timing fits a market that is changing shape. As we reported on 24 November, Illinois regulators have just issued 148 new medical cannabis dispensary licences, taking the statewide total to 220. More storefronts mean more shelf space to fill, and an operator that grows its own product can capture margin that would otherwise go to wholesale suppliers.

The price is small by the standards of recent multistate deals. At $6.5 million, the Illinois purchase is about one-sixth of the roughly $40 million Jushi expects to spend expanding its Manassas, Virginia facility. That gap suggests the company is buying an existing licensed site rather than building one from scratch.
> Jushi is paying for Illinois with a lender's consent and planning Virginia on a mortgage: growth funded carefully, one facility at a time.
## How the deal is being paid for

Jushi's lender group, with FG Agency Lending LLC acting as agent, has agreed to a second amendment to the company's 27 March 2026 loan agreement, which Jushi disclosed in an 8-K filing on 20 November. Under that amendment the agent consented to the Illinois acquisition, subject to conditions, and the lenders may provide up to $4.25 million in additional term loans to help pay for it. Jushi stressed that this extra lending is uncommitted, but said it expects it to be funded on or about 4 December 2026.

On those figures, the new term loans could cover about 65% of the $6.5 million price, with the rest coming from Jushi's own resources. Jushi did not name the seller or the facility's location within Illinois.

The company is also reworking other debt. It is negotiating a five-year extension of the mortgage on its Arlington, Virginia property, which has about $6.3 million of principal outstanding, and expects to sign it before the end of 2026. Separately, it is talking to some noteholders about extending part of the acquisition-related debt that falls due in the quarter ending 30 June 2027.
## The Virginia bet

Virginia is where most of the new money would go. Jushi said it is negotiating to expand its existing Manassas mortgage by as much as $15 million to $20 million. The full Manassas expansion is expected to cost about $40 million, with construction starting in late 2026 or early 2027 and taking about 12 months. Jushi said loan proceeds would cover part of the bill and operating cash flow or other sources the rest, and that it can slow the pace of spending if needed.

Two smaller projects are closer to done. Improvements to the existing warehouse at Manassas are nearing completion and awaiting regulatory approvals, and the company has filed for permits. Once finished, Jushi expects the site to roughly double its indoor biomass production capacity in Virginia. A separate greenhouse project remains on schedule to be ready in the first quarter of 2027.

The reason for the rush is the calendar. Jushi said adult-use sales in Virginia begin on 1 July 2027, and it operates six dispensaries in the state. On the company's timeline, construction finishing in late 2027 or early 2028 means the full Manassas expansion would not be ready for the first months of adult-use trading, so the greenhouse and warehouse work are what Jushi can bring to bear at launch.
## October numbers and a governance change

Jushi also released preliminary, unaudited figures for October 2026. Net revenue was about $23.39 million, up 4.6% from about $22.37 million a year earlier. Gross profit rose 21.4% to about $11.37 million, lifting gross margin to 48.6% from 41.9%. By our arithmetic, that is a margin gain of 6.7 percentage points on only modest sales growth, which suggests costs, not volume, are doing most of the work.

The release also disclosed that on 23 November Jushi and its chief executive, chairman and founder, James Cacioppo, amended and restated his options and warrants to add a cap: he may not exercise them if doing so would give him beneficial ownership above 19.99%, pending approval by shareholders as required by the Canadian Securities Exchange. The change covers 6,000,000 options and 20,735,239 warrants, or about 26.7 million instruments in total. Jushi said the change is a related-party transaction under Canadian rules, that its audit committee and board approved it, and that Cacioppo abstained.
## What to watch

The first date to watch is on or about 4 December, when Jushi expects the extra term loans to be funded. Next is the signing of the Arlington mortgage extension and any agreement on the larger Manassas mortgage, both of which Jushi hopes to complete by late 2026 or early 2027. Illinois regulatory approval of the facility transfer, expected to allow closing in the first quarter of 2027, will decide when Jushi can start supplying its own Illinois stores. And in Virginia, the 1 July 2027 adult-use start is the date by which the warehouse and greenhouse capacity needs to be producing.
